title: What Scripture Actually Means by Killing Your Self-Pity
caption:
What Scripture actually means by killing your self-pity. It's not a mood. It's a sin like any other.

Self-pity feels like just being real about how hard things are. It's actually pride wearing a sad face, insisting your situation is the exception to everyone else's rules. Philippians 2:14 doesn't leave a rough-week exception. Do everything without grumbling means everything, including today.

Self-pity always needs someone to measure against. Cut the scroll that's feeding it before you try to pray it away. And say it out loud to one man: I've been feeling sorry for myself instead of trusting God with this. It loses power the second it has a name.

Where's self-pity been running your week instead of God?
